title: feat: GitHub Copilot CLI (`copilot`) as a fifth agent provider: Agents menu and settings, both wrappers, the moe and Serena MCP servers
definitionOfDone: Choosing Copilot in the JetBrains Agents menu, or agentCommand `copilot`, launches a copilot seat through both wrappers, one-shot and headless per task, with the moe and Serena MCP servers. A recorded real-CLI smoke on Windows and in WSL claims, works and completes a scratch task.
worker.type is COPILOT end to end: the proxy's MOE_WORKER_TYPE, the daemon record and the board. VS Code offers the same provider.
A flag the installed copilot rejects stops the seat with MOE_CLI_ARGV_REJECTED, not a relaunch loop, and a missing CLI or sign-in gives one coded line. Tested in both wrappers.
Under executionProfile verified-local, a copilot worker or QA seat is refused (MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_CLI_UNSUPPORTED), unless the plan documents and tests another behavior.
scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes. Postflight harness rows cover copilot in both wrappers. ./gradlew test and the VS Code tests pass.
Docs updated: the per-CLI launch section of scripts/CLAUDE.md, CONFIGURATION.md (agentCommand), the README provider list and the docs/PRD.md row.

implementationPlan.description:
Create scripts/tests/copilot-smoke.mjs with your own Write tool (a TOOL witness; never a shell write, per the global rail). It is the repeatable real-CLI smoke for DoD 1-2. Model it on scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs: free-port `daemon init --project

--port `, the /health wait, a proxy-stdio MCP client with `ws` loaded via createRequire(proxyEntry), board WebSocket APPROVE_TASK with expectedPlanRevision, and `daemon stop --project` in finally. Copy those helpers; never import onboarding.mjs, which runs on import. Facts: mem:decision-copilot-cli-contract. USAGE: `node scripts/tests/copilot-smoke.mjs [--command ] [--keep]`. defaults to `copilot`; anything else exits 2 with a usage line. Run it from a snapshot whose packages/moe-daemon/dist and packages/moe-proxy/dist are built, and assert both, as onboarding does. - sh needs a non-win32 platform. It launches `bash /scripts/moe-agent.sh --role worker --project

--worker-id smoke-copilot-sh --command --no-loop --no-interactive`, the JetBrains bash shape for a copilot worker. - ps1 needs win32. It launches `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "& '\scripts\moe-agent.ps1' -Role worker -Project '

' -WorkerId smoke-copilot-ps1 -Command '' -NoLoop -Interactive:$false; exit $LASTEXITCODE"`. That is Windows PowerShell 5.1 and JetBrains' `&` call (TerminalAgentLauncher.kt about :778). -File cannot bind -Interactive:$false on 5.1. CHILD ENV: process.env minus every MOE_* key except MOE_SERENA_PATH, and minus CLAUDE* keys. The driver runs inside a live seat whose MOE_WORKER_ID, MOE_SESSION_ID and MOE_ATTEMPT_* must never reach the scratch seat or its proxy. Keep HOME/USERPROFILE: copilot's sign-in and Serena live there. Keep the inherited GIT_CONFIG_* keys, because the wrapper appends its own guard entry to GIT_CONFIG_COUNT (moe-agent.sh about :9632). Only the scratch daemon gets HOME/USERPROFILE = /profile, so it never writes the human's ~/.moe. FIXTURE: - scratch = mkdtemp(os.tmpdir(), 'moe-copilot-smoke-'), and P = /project. - In P: `git init -b main`, a local user.name/user.email, a .gitignore with .moe/ .mcp.json .serena/ .worktrees/, and a README.md seed commit. - canary = 'CANARY-' + 16 hex chars from crypto.randomBytes, written to P/.serena/memories/smoke-canary.md. - Through the daemon and proxy: create_epic; create_task with DoD 'proof.txt holds the smoke-canary memory'; set_task_status PLANNING; create_team architect plus join_team smoke-architect; claim by taskId; get_context. - submit_plan with ONE step, newFiles ['proof.txt'] and the description "Read the memory named smoke-canary with the serena MCP server's read_memory tool (do not open files under .serena yourself), then create proof.txt in the project root whose whole content is exactly that memory's text." - Then APPROVE_TASK over /ws until get_context reports WORKING. RUN: - Spawn the wrapper and record its PID; on POSIX it is detached in its own process group. - Tee stdout and stderr to /wrapper.log and to the console, bounded by SMOKE_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 900). - On timeout, kill only that recorded child: on POSIX process.kill(-pid,'SIGTERM'), then SIGKILL after 5 s; on Windows `taskkill /PID /T /F`. Never kill by name or pattern (global rail). - While it runs, call moe.list_workers every 2 s and record each `type` of the seat's record (its id; else the record whose currentTaskId is the smoke task). - Also record payload.type of every /ws WORKER_CREATED, WORKER_UPDATED and STATE_SNAPSHOT worker for that seat. That is the feed the board's WorkerPanel titles cards with (AccountPresentation.workerTitle). VERDICT, checked in this order: (1) BLOCKED, exit 3, when wrapper.log holds a line with MOE_COPILOT_NOT_FOUND, MOE_COPILOT_SIGNED_OUT, MOE_COPILOT_NOT_ENTITLED, MOE_COPILOT_MCP_BLOCKED or `MOE_CLI_ARGV_REJECTED: the installed copilot`. Print `BLOCKED copilot-smoke : `. This is a human prerequisite, never a pass. (2) PASS, exit 0, only when ALL of these hold: - the wrapper exited 0; - get_context shows REVIEW or DONE and every plan step COMPLETED; - `git -C P log --all` has a feat(task-) or fix(task-) completion commit whose proof.txt (`git show :proof.txt`, trimmed) equals the canary; - the seat's last daemon-record type before deregistration is COPILOT, and so is at least one /ws worker event; - a Serena log /.serena/logs//mcp_*.txt, with mtime at or after the launch, holds `read_memory: memory_name='smoke-canary'` (Serena logs each tool call that way). Then print ONE line: `PASS copilot-smoke : copilot --version`>; task ; steps /; worker type COPILOT (daemon ; board ); commit ; canary ok; serena read_memory ok (); s`. (3) Otherwise FAIL, exit 1: `FAIL copilot-smoke : `, plus the last 60 lines of wrapper.log. ERROR HANDLING: - Every await and child has a bound. A daemon that never turns healthy, a refused tool call or a git failure is a FAIL with its reason, never a hang or a PASS. - finally always closes the board socket and the proxy, runs `daemon stop --project P`, and removes scratch, unless --keep, which prints the kept path. Use rmSync with maxRetries for Windows EBUSY, behind onboarding's guard: dirname is os.tmpdir() and the basename prefix matches. - Never read ~/.copilot or any credential file, and never print env values. - ` --version` on win32 needs spawnSync(..., {shell: true}) for npm's .cmd shim. This file is not a *.test.mjs, so ci-workflows.test.mjs's CI-wiring rule does not apply (precedent: onboarding.mjs, wave1-pilot.mjs). Its offline regression test is leg P of step 2's gate.

Create scripts/tests/copilot-final-gate.sh with your Write tool. It is this epic-final row's regression gate, and checkRefs[0] runs it as `timeout 1200s bash ...` from the repo or task-worktree root on a /mnt/<drive> path.
SETUP:
- Resolve ROOT from BASH_SOURCE and cd there, then `unset ${!MOE_*} ${!CLAUDE*} ${!FAKE_*}`.
- Require node, npm, git, wslpath, cmd.exe, powershell.exe and pwsh.exe. A missing one exits 2 naming it; never a SKIP.
- Reach Windows through `/init "$(command -v cmd.exe)"`, which works whether or not WSL's binfmt entry is registered (mem:gotcha-wsl-interop-binfmt-init).
- Print first: `[gate] the JetBrains leg needs the caller to hold the jetbrains-gradle lease`.
LEG D, docs: run it first and synchronously, but let the other legs run whatever it says. A small `node - <<'JS'` check prints `DOCS STALE: <file>: <needle>` for each miss. Needles per file:
- scripts/CLAUDE.md: MOE_COPILOT_NOT_FOUND, MOE_COPILOT_CONFIG_FAILED, MOE_COPILOT_SIGNED_OUT, MOE_COPILOT_NOT_ENTITLED, MOE_COPILOT_MCP_BLOCKED, `copilot-smoke.mjs`, `All five CLIs`, `Grok, Copilot or interactive Claude`.
- docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md: the same five codes, plus `MOE_CLI_ARGV_REJECTED: the installed copilot`.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md: MOE_COPILOT_MODEL, MOE_COPILOT_EFFORT, '`GROK` or `COPILOT`', '`copilot` → `COPILOT`', and the line starting '| `agentCommand` |' must contain '`copilot`'.
- docs/SCHEMA.md: `GROK or COPILOT`.
- README.md and docs/PRD.md: `GitHub Copilot CLI` (task-1c580985's text); docs/PRD.md must not contain `Autocomplete only`.
THEN FOUR PARALLEL LEGS. Each runs in a subshell that writes $L/<leg>.log; record each PID and collect its exit code with `wait <pid>`.
- W, wrappers: `bash scripts/tests/copilot-guards-gate.sh`, task-e266a150's gate: vm-route on bash, 5.1 and pwsh 7 with every copilot row of ab323f85, 49d4a565 and d0ea8735; bash -n and ParseFile; both parity checks; lint; its mutation rows. It must print `PASS copilot-guards-gate`. Use the landed file name. Then `node --test scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs` (bash rows: CP1, CP2 and the five-name refusal).
- J, JetBrains: `/init "$(command -v cmd.exe)" /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d <wslpath -w ROOT>\moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test --rerun"`. WSL has no JDK (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-from-wsl). Then require TEST-*.xml under moe-jetbrains/build/test-results/test newer than the leg's start, with tests > 0 and failures + errors = 0, so an UP-TO-DATE run cannot pass.
- V, VS Code: S = `mktemp -d` outside the checkout, then `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C $S`. Use the whole repo, because its tests read JetBrains and daemon sources. Then in $S/moe-vscode run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm test && npm run compile`.
- P, packages and the smoke driver, in the same $S:
  - copy this task's scripts/tests/copilot-smoke.mjs over the snapshot's (it is uncommitted in the worktree);
  - in $S/packages/moe-proxy: `npm ci && npm run build`;
  - in $S/packages/moe-daemon: `npm ci && npm run build && npx vitest run src/tools/workerType.test.ts`;
  - then `timeout 300 node $S/scripts/tests/copilot-smoke.mjs sh --command $S/no-such-dir/copilot` must exit 3 with one `BLOCKED copilot-smoke sh: ` line naming MOE_COPILOT_NOT_FOUND.
  That last check is the driver's offline test: a real daemon, board, fixture, wrapper pre-flight and claim, with no model call.
OUTPUT: print `tail -n 15` of each leg's log, a per-leg PASS/FAIL table and the elapsed seconds. Print `PASS copilot-final-gate` and exit 0 only when D and all four legs pass. Otherwise exit 1 and keep $L, printing its path.
ERROR HANDLING:
- A trap on EXIT, INT and TERM kills only the recorded leg PIDs (never by name or pattern, per the global rail) and removes only its own $S.
- npm runs only in $S, never in the shared checkout (global rail).
- No full postflight.{sh,ps1} (gate-budget rail).
TEST IT NOW: bash -n the file, take the jetbrains-gradle lease (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease), and run it once. Expect only leg D red (docs not written yet: the docs RED) and W, J, V and P green, inside 20 minutes. Record the wall time, then release the lease.

Docs, scripts/CLAUDE.md, with the Edit tool. A Bash or python doc edit leaves no TOOL witness (mem:gotcha-docs-edit-via-bash-python-no-tool-witness). First read the landed copilot blocks in scripts/moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 (tasks ab323f85, 49d4a565 and d0ea8735) and copy every flag, code, banner and env name from there, never from this plan.
(a) Per-CLI launch: add one new paragraph after the existing one. Cover:
- Selection: agentCommand `copilot`, or any path whose base name is copilot (.exe/.cmd stripped); npm `@github/copilot`.
- Role polarity as claude and grok: an architect or governor TUI, worker and qa headless. --interactive/--no-interactive (ps1 -Interactive / -Interactive:$false) override it. No exec flag. Polling is off for a copilot TUI.
- The exact landed headless argv. The prompt rides stdin, never argv, as UTF-8 on every PowerShell engine. Each launch gets a private --log-dir and MCP JSON. The TUI argv has no --allow-all or --no-ask-user and adds -i <pointer>.
- The guards: the once-per-process argv probe (MOE_CLI_ARGV_REJECTED; MOE_DISABLE_ARGV_PROBE=1 skips it), MOE_COPILOT_NOT_FOUND, MOE_COPILOT_CONFIG_FAILED, MOE_COPILOT_SIGNED_OUT, MOE_COPILOT_NOT_ENTITLED and MOE_COPILOT_MCP_BLOCKED. Each prints one line, escalates once to #general and exits 1, never a relaunch loop.
- Sign-in: COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN; else `copilot login`, kept in the OS keychain (WSL has none, so plaintext ~/.copilot/config.json); else gh's. Windows and WSL sign in separately. The account's Copilot plan must include Copilot CLI, and its policy must allow third-party MCP servers.
- Model and effort: --model only when explicit (-Model/--model, settings.models.{role}, else MOE_COPILOT_MODEL; never the claude fallback). --reasoning-effort comes from MOE_COPILOT_EFFORT, else the claimed task's launch effort, else nothing. Copilot takes none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh and max; which ones work depends on the model.
- No TOOL witness: the text output carries no machine-readable tool events, so copilot lands like Gemini and Grok. No Claude account rotation. Under verified-local, a copilot worker or QA seat is refused (MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_CLI_UNSUPPORTED).
- `scripts/tests/copilot-smoke.mjs` runs the real-CLI smoke. Step 5 appends the closing `Verified ...` sentence.
(b) In the Land-on-every-exit TOOL tier, `a Codex TUI, Gemini, Grok or interactive Claude session leaves none` becomes `a Codex TUI, Gemini, Grok, Copilot or interactive Claude session leaves none`.
(c) In the MCP-servers bullet, add copilot's config: a per-launch JSON in the wrapper's private temp dir, passed as --additional-mcp-config @<file> with --disable-builtin-mcps.

- Server serena runs with --context agent on the launch's Serena root (W in worktree mode).
Then `**All four CLIs**` becomes `**All five CLIs**`, and the Serena --context list becomes `claude-code`/`codex`/`agent`/`agent`/`agent` for claude/codex/gemini/grok/copilot.

Real-CLI smoke (DoD 1 and 2), once per engine, WSL first. It spends real Copilot premium requests: run each engine once, and again only after a fix.
PRECONDITIONS are the human's, not yours: copilot installed and signed in on that OS, with an account whose Copilot plan includes Copilot CLI and whose policy allows MCP servers. - PASS (exit 0): post ONE task comment with both PASS lines verbatim, both copilot versions and the UTC date. Then append to scripts/CLAUDE.md's copilot paragraph, with the Edit tool: `Verified <UTC date> with copilot <version> on WSL (bash) and Windows (PowerShell 5.1) by scripts/tests/copilot-smoke.mjs.`
- BLOCKED (exit 3) is a human prerequisite. Post the BLOCKED line(s) as a task comment. Then call moe.report_blocked {taskId, reason: '<BLOCKED line>; human action: <the remedy that code's TROUBLESHOOTING entry names>', needsFrom: 'human', blockedOnTaskIds: []} and end the session. Steps 1-4 are already checkpointed, and the next session reruns this step.
- FAIL (exit 1): rerun once with --keep, then read the scratch dir and wrapper.log.
  - A defect in this task's own driver is fixed here, in scripts/tests/copilot-smoke.mjs.
  - A defect in a landed slice is NOT patched here. Examples: the @file servers do not load in an untrusted folder, the tools are unreachable, or the prompt is not read. Create ONE bug task in epic-be924fb8 with the evidence: the copilot version, the failing check, log excerpts with no secrets, and the wrapper lines and vm-route rows involved. Then call moe.report_blocked {blockedOnTaskIds: [<that id>]} so this row resumes when it lands.
Error handling for an interrupted run: the driver stops its own daemon and child. If a session dies mid-run, remove only the scratch dir it printed. Never claim a PASS you did not see, never weaken a driver check to get one, and never paste tokens, ~/.copilot contents or env values anywhere.

Verification. Take the jetbrains-gradle lease with moe.acquire_resource {resourceId: 'jetbrains-gradle', taskId, workerId, note: 'copilot-final-gate'}. This gate re-proves DoD 2-6 at the integrated tip: docs anchors, every copilot row of both wrappers on bash, 5.1 and pwsh 7, both parity checks, lint, protected-agent-command, ./gradlew test, the VS Code tests and compile, the daemon worker-type test, and the driver's offline row.
Error handling for a red run:
- Read the failing leg's log (the gate prints its path), then rerun that leg's command alone to diagnose.
- Leg D is this task's docs: fix them.
- A failure in leg W, J or V caused by a slice's landed code becomes a bug task, as in step 5. Never edit wrappers, harnesses or IDE code in this row.
- Never substitute a smaller gate, never run the full postflight, and never run npm in the shared checkout.

Adversarial self-review: load adversarial-self-review. The scope is the whole Copilot feature: this task's diff plus the landed commits of bfadf533, ab323f85, 49d4a565, e266a150, d0ea8735, d609eae3, 7739d4af, 1c580985 and 3a531816. The Stability & Hardening epic's other rows already passed their own gates.
Check:
(1) Twin parity of every copilot string in both wrappers. parity-check passes, but read the hunks anyway.
(2) The driver:
- the identity scrub: no MOE_WORKER_ID, MOE_SESSION_ID or MOE_ATTEMPT_* reaches the scratch seat;
- every wait is bounded, only the owned PID is ever killed, and the scratch-removal guard holds;
- no credential reads;
- the verdict order: a NOT_FOUND line can never PASS, and a seat that completes without calling Serena FAILs.
(3) The gate: every leg's exit code is collected; an UP-TO-DATE Gradle run or a SKIP cannot count green; the trap kills only its own PIDs; nothing builds in the shared checkout.
(4) Docs: every code, flag, banner and env name matches the landed wrappers byte for byte (grep each one). Nothing promises more than the landed behavior, and the measured 1.0.106 facts are labeled as measured.
(5) Verified-local: read the wrapper's verified-local gate and confirm it applies to the qa role too. vm-route row C3 covers worker; d0ea8735's plan adds a qa row; the IDE slices refuse both roles. If no row covers a copilot QA seat, file a bug task.
(6) Concurrency: two smokes at once use separate scratch dirs and ports, and each gate run gets its own snapshot.
(7) Cross-platform: Windows paths with spaces in the driver's quoted -Command, CRLF-safe docs, and moe-agent.ps1's BOM untouched.
Fix what you find in this task's files and rerun checkRefs[0]. Anything in a slice's files becomes a bug task. No added line may contain a project.json globalRails.forbiddenPatterns string.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: GitHub Copilot CLI is a fifth agent provider end to end. The slice rows' wrappers, IDE pickers, daemon worker type and listings are integrated, and a repeatable real-CLI smoke proves them on WSL (the bash wrapper) and on Windows (moe-agent.ps1 on Windows PowerShell 5.1). In each smoke a copilot worker seat claims, works and completes a scratch task through the moe and Serena MCP servers, with worker.type COPILOT on the daemon record and on the board feed. The epic-final gate re-runs every affected suite within 20 minutes. scripts/CLAUDE.md, CONFIGURATION.md, SCHEMA.md and TROUBLESHOOTING.md document the landed behavior and the measured copilot 1.0.106 contract.
acceptanceCriteria: checkRefs[1] (WSL, bash wrapper) and checkRefs[2] (Windows, moe-agent.ps1 on Windows PowerShell 5.1) each print `PASS copilot-smoke <engine>`. Each run shows: the task in REVIEW or DONE with every step COMPLETED; a completion commit whose proof.txt equals the canary; worker.type COPILOT on the daemon record and on the /ws board feed; and Serena's own log showing read_memory smoke-canary. checkRefs[0] prints `PASS copilot-final-gate` within 20 minutes. It covers: the docs anchors; copilot-guards-gate.sh (vm-route on bash, 5.1 and pwsh 7 with every copilot row, parse checks, parity-check.sh and .ps1, lint); protected-agent-command (bash rows); ./gradlew test with fresh XML and zero failures; the VS Code npm test and compile; the daemon's workerType.test.ts; and the driver's offline NOT_FOUND row exiting 3.

A human-side prerequisite makes the driver print one BLOCKED line and exit 3, never PASS. These are: a missing CLI, a signed-out CLI, an account without Copilot CLI, MCP servers blocked by policy, or an argv rejection. The row is then reported blocked on the named human action.

moe.list_workers returns each worker's type. /ws broadcasts WORKER_CREATED and WORKER_UPDATED with the full Worker (WebSocketServer.broadcast). The JetBrains WorkerPanel titles each card with worker.type (AccountPresentation.workerTitle).
Serena logs each tool call as `read_memory: memory_name='<name>'` in ~/.serena/logs/<date>/mcp_*.txt. Windows has %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\serena.exe and node.exe.
Worker claude seats run with --permission-mode bypassPermissions (moe-agent.sh PRINT_ARGS), so a worker may launch `copilot --allow-all`. The interactive architect TUI's classifier refused that run.
WSL has no JDK, so Gradle runs as gradlew.bat through cmd.exe. `gradlew test` needs no daemon or proxy dist, because requireBundledAssets runs only in prepareSandbox.
The wrapper appends its git-guard entry to an inherited GIT_CONFIG_COUNT (moe-agent.sh about :9632).
JetBrains runs the ps1 wrapper as `& <script> -Role ... -Command <cmd>` (TerminalAgentLauncher.kt about :778). task-d609eae3 adds `-Interactive:$false` for copilot.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A manual smoke procedure recorded only in a comment: rejected. QA could not re-run it, and it is not repeatable for the next copilot version. A driver modeled on onboarding.mjs makes the smoke a command (checkRefs[1]/[2]). The driver's NOT_FOUND path doubles as an offline regression row inside the gate.
- An inline checkRefs[0] that chains wrappers, Gradle, VS Code and daemon legs: rejected. It cannot fit the 1000-char cap with the docs anchors. An owned gate script reuses e266a150's copilot-guards-gate.sh for the wrapper leg instead.
- Patching any wrapper defect the smoke finds in this row: rejected. The wrappers' argv is pinned by vm-route rows from other rows, and this row would grow past 6 files. A defect becomes a bug task, and this row blocks on it.
- A JSONL TOOL witness (`--output-format json`): deferred. The wrapper runs text mode, no tool-event shape was measurable without an entitled account, and in worktree mode attribution has no tiers. Copilot lands like Gemini and Grok.
- A new guard row, task-d0ea8735, was filed from the measured 403 and MCP-policy failures, and this row depends on it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The board's worker cards show worker.type raw (WorkerPanel via AccountPresentation.workerTitle), fed by /ws WORKER_CREATED/WORKER_UPDATED. So recording the /ws events proves the board leg of DoD 2, and moe.list_workers proves the daemon record.
- Serena logs every tool application with its arguments, so a read_memory of a unique memory name proves the serena server was used.
- The wrapper's git guard appends to an inherited GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, so the driver can keep the live seat's overlay.
- Gradle must run through cmd.exe from WSL. A fresh worktree has no build dir, so a Kotlin compile adds about 1-2 min.
- The verified-local CLI check is one catch-all for worker and QA seats (moe-agent.sh about :10243). The harness rows cover worker only; d0ea8735's plan adds a qa row.
planningNotes.risks:
- The human must sign in, in WSL and in Windows after installing copilot there, with an account that has Copilot CLI and allows MCP servers. On 2026-11-06 the WSL account failed both, so the smoke reports BLOCKED until then.
- The smoke spends premium requests: run each engine once.
- Copilot behavior was not measurable without an entitled run: @file MCP servers in an untrusted prompt-mode folder, env propagation to MCP servers, tool naming, and per-model effort support. The smoke settles them, and a failure routes to a bug task.
- Gate wall time: the W leg (vm-route on three engines) dominates at about 10 min; the other legs run in parallel. Hold the jetbrains-gradle lease.
- Windows snapshot builds on drvfs are slow, and rm -rf there takes minutes.
- If e266a150 landed its gate under another name, the gate script uses the landed one (it is this task's own file).
